changes: Date: the chronogram kha(0)-candra(1)-vasu(8), read right to left, gives only 810. The reading Śaka 1810 assumes an omitted digit or millennium, which the notes now say.
Date: nakshatra_yoga now records that the yoga name is corrupt ('yogagāḍhyaṃ'); only Hasta is certain.
Notes: 'ravau karkaṭa(ke) kanyāyāṃ indur' (sun in Cancer, moon in Virgo) is consistent with Hasta and with Śrāvaṇa śukla 5, so the month reading 'name' = nabhe (Śrāvaṇa) is supported.
Notes: the conversion to 12 August 1888 is not verified against an ephemeris.
Persons: Medinīrāja lowered to medium confidence because 'sūnumedinīrājakaḥ' is run together in the text. The '-ka' ending is taken as a suffix added to the name, not part of it.

date.as_written: khacandravasusakasyāt name śukleśu pañcamī || hastarkṣe yogagāḍhyaṃ(!) ca vāre ravi ... ravau(!) karkaṭakanyāyāṃ indurgatimibhāṃvasaḥ(!)
date.nakshatra_yoga: Hasta (moon in Kanyā, sun in Karkaṭa); yoga name corrupt ('gāḍhyaṃ')

notes: The chronogram kha-candra-vasu (0-1-8, read right to left) gives Śaka 810. This is impossible for a Devanagari paper manuscript, so a digit or the millennium was probably left out, giving Śaka 1810 (about 1888 CE). The ce_approx is therefore an inference. 'name' is most likely a corruption of 'nabhe' (Śrāvaṇa). This fits the planetary data: sun in Karkaṭa, moon in Kanyā (Hasta) on śukla 5. The exact Julian date (12 August 1888, a Sunday) has not been checked against an ephemeris. 'yogagāḍhyaṃ' is corrupt and the yoga name cannot be recovered with confidence. The phrase 'śrīgovinda ... bhūt' has a lacuna and is an invocation, not a person. The final 'samvat' is blank.
